title: Chapter 38
content:
Jakyeong’s eyes darted with frantic, silent calculation.

"I have no idea what you're talking about, Director Kang."

"Of course you don't."

In a lightning-fast motion, Il-hyun plucked the sunglasses from Jakyeong’s face. The raw, murderous intent burning in those dark eyes was a far cry from the fragile persona of Jang Yi-an. But to Il-hyun, this unmasked version was infinitely more intoxicating. There was nothing quite like the thrill of breaking a feral beast and forcing it onto its knees.

"I heard a very amusing piece of gossip during my trip to Hong Kong."

Il-hyun paused, wetting his lower lip with the tip of his tongue. Jakyeong kept his mouth clamped shut, a cold sweat breaking out across his spine.

"I was agonizing over how to confront you about it... and then you magically appear aboard this ship. Quite convenient, wouldn't you say?"

"..."

"Aren't you curious to know what that amusing story was?"

Il-hyun maintained a bright, delighted smile, like a man bearing joyful news, while Jakyeong stood in suffocating silence.

"Word is... someone wants me dead. And they sent an assassin right under my roof."

Behind his back, Jakyeong’s fingers clenched into a white-knuckled fist. He knows everything. How?

Il-hyun gently cupped Jakyeong’s cheek in a warm, possessive hold. "Go on, explain yourself. I'll listen first before deciding whether to play the fool."

Eight days remained until the scheduled execution date, but with the cover blown to shreds, options were non-existent. Catching the lethal predator gleaming beneath Il-hyun’s smiling eyes, Jakyeong knew feigning ignorance was useless.

Jakyeong drove his shoulder forward with explosive force, shoving Il-hyun back.

Capitalizing on the momentary gap, he whipped a combat dagger from his inner lining and lunged. The steel blade sliced through the air in a lethal arc aimed straight at Il-hyun's throat.

Il-hyun snapped his head back, letting the edge graze his collar, and caught Jakyeong’s forearm mid-strike.

Jakyeong transferred the blade to his left hand in a seamless, fluid pass, driving the point downward toward Il-hyun's arm. As Il-hyun grabbed that wrist to intercept, Jakyeong channeled his entire momentum, driving him back into the wall.

The back of Il-hyun's shoulders slammed against the bulkhead. The tip of the blade halted bare millimeters below his Adam's apple.

Jakyeong leaned his full body weight into the hilt, but the raw disparity in physical strength was overwhelming. With their arms locked in a brutal stalemate, Jakyeong shifted his left hand behind the pommel, pressing down with his palm. Inch by grueling inch, the steel point edged closer to the carotid artery.

Even with the cold steel hovering over his jugular, not a single trace of panic crossed Il-hyun’s face. Instead, a razor-thin, mocking smirk touched his lips.

"You really don't want to do this."

With that low warning, Il-hyun surged with monstrous leverage, wrenching his arms outward to break the lock.

Finding himself overpowered, Jakyeong snapped his forehead forward, delivering a brutal headbutt straight into the bridge of Il-hyun's nose.

Il-hyun cursed under his breath, stumbling as his hand flew to his bloody nose. Jakyeong lunged with the blade once more, but Il-hyun ducked beneath the thrust, driving his shoulder into Jakyeong’s midsection and slamming him against the opposing wall.

In the ensuing struggle, Il-hyun seized Jakyeong’s weapon hand and violently twisted the wrist.

A sharp, breathless grunt tore from Jakyeong’s throat as the joint strained. Pressed flush from chest to thigh, Jakyeong couldn't even chamber a knee strike.

"That's enough," Il-hyun whispered smoothly against his ear. "Shouldn't you show a little more deference to your new employer?"

The words brought Jakyeong to a sudden, rigid halt.

"What the hell are you talking about?"

"Did you not hear me? I am informing you that your contracting client has officially changed—from my father, to me."

Jakyeong’s brow furrowed in disbelief. What kind of madness was this? More importantly, Kang Il-hyun was already fully aware that his own father had put out the contract on his life.

Judging by the unblinking calm in his dark eyes, it was no bluff.

"Dmitri, was it? Quite a reasonable fellow once you speak his language."

Il-hyun let out a low chuckle as he dropped the broker's name.

Hearing that specific identity slip past Il-hyun's lips made Jakyeong’s face turn stark and pale. This wasn't an interrogation tactic or a lucky guess.

"So... how about putting the blade away? Before I run out of patience."

Their gazes clashed in a silent, suffocating war of nerves.

Just then, Wang Ryun’s voice crackled through the encrypted earpiece in Jakyeong’s ear. Jakyeong remained frozen, keeping the knife poised.

[Jakyeong! Do you copy?]

Releasing his rigid posture, Il-hyun relaxed his grip and leaned back against the wall, watching Jakyeong with amused detachment. Jakyeong took two slow, cautious steps backward, maintaining his combat stance.

Il-hyun reached up, wincing slightly as he rubbed his bruised nose.

"I hear you," Jakyeong muttered into the mic, keeping his eyes glued to Il-hyun. "Go ahead."

[What took you so long to answer? Where are you?]

"Still aboard the ship."

[Should I come back in to extract you?]

Jakyeong’s gaze lingered on the man standing before him. "No. I'll be out shortly. Hold your position."

Ending the transmission, Jakyeong kept his guard raised.

Il-hyun produced a fresh cigarette, sparked the tip, and extended it toward him. "Still suffering from weak lungs?"

Jakyeong ignored the cigarette, glaring with pure venom. "How did you find out?"

"There are many ways to unearth the truth," Il-hyun drawled. "Though it did cost me a rather hefty sum."

"I haven't received confirmation that the contract transferred."

"Which is precisely why I am presenting the offer to you in person."

"I have zero interest in accepting your proposal." Jakyeong tightened his grip around the hilt.

"Don't waste your energy on pointless defiance. I haven't finished explaining the terms."

"..."

"I'm not asking you to assassinate my father. All you have to do... is shoot me on the scheduled date, exactly as planned."

The proposition sounded entirely unhinged.

"What kind of twisted game is this?"

"Exactly what you just heard. Naturally, I will double your payout. And I will personally guarantee your safe extraction and immunity afterward."

As the pieces fell into place, Jakyeong realized the monstrous calculation behind the plot. Kang Il-hyun intended to take a non-lethal bullet to manufacture the ultimate, bulletproof justification to purge Chairman Kang and seize total control of Haewon Group. If Il-hyun had enough intelligence to unmask Jakyeong, he undoubtedly possessed forensic proof that his father had orchestrated the hit.

The true scale of the man's ambition was finally laid bare.

Il-hyun’s gaze softened into something disturbingly tender. "I'll give you time to consider it. Your friend seems to be waiting outside, so we'll conclude our business for tonight."

"And if I refuse?"

"You won't," Il-hyun smiled with absolute certainty. "You're far too intelligent for that. And you have a healthy appreciation for money."

With a languid chuckle, Il-hyun closed the distance between them.

Jakyeong’s fingers tightened on the hilt. Stopping bare inches away, Il-hyun tilted his head, his dark eyes narrowing into a sharp, predatory focus.

He reached out. When Jakyeong swatted at his wrist with the flat of the blade, Il-hyun bypassed the guard with fluid speed, his fingers catching the corner of the bandage on Jakyeong’s neck and ripping it clean off.

The exposed crimson bruise caught the light.

The calm, mocking amusement that had remained unshakable even under the threat of a blade evaporated in an instant. Il-hyun’s eyes turned lethally, terrifyingly dark.

Jakyeong shoved him back, snatched the fallen adhesive, and smoothed it over the mark. When he looked away, Il-hyun’s large hand shot out, clamping around his throat with suffocating force.

"Seems you had quite a lively time while I was away."

The voice was dripping with venomous, arctic malice.

Jakyeong wrenched himself free from the grip with a violent twist, glaring back. Why the bastard was taking personal offense was utterly baffling.

Yet in the next breath, Il-hyun curled his lips into a polished, model-ready smile.

"Shall we head out? It would be rather inconvenient if we bumped into Choi Ki-tae together."

Beneath the polite words, the look in his eyes was as frigid as a winter blizzard.

Standing motionless beneath the cascade of hot water, Jakyeong let the stream wash over him for a long time. Even after scrubbing away the salt of the sea, the phantom metallic stench of blood seemed to cling to his skin.

Once the corridors had thinned out, Il-hyun had escorted him directly to the upper deck. Despite the syndicate boss being executed in his private quarters, the vessel had remained eerily subdued. As anticipated, Choi Ki-tae was actively suppressing the news of his father's demise to prevent a panic among their elite clientele.

Jakyeong had rappelled down the hull into the dark waters, swimming to the extraction boat idling off the starboard quarter. Kang Il-hyun had remained stationed at the ship's railing, watching in silence until Jakyeong hauled himself aboard.

Shutting off the water and toweling dry, Jakyeong stepped out into the garage apartment.

Wang Ryun approached with an unlit cigarette dangling from his lips, holding a handful of pain-relief patches. While Jakyeong had avoided knife wounds, his body was battered with deep contusions, and he had been lost in a daze ever since pulling himself out of the water.

"Did something go sideways on that ship?" Ryun asked.

Jakyeong shook his head.

Upon reaching the safehouse, he had immediately dialed Wang Han, but his handler was completely oblivious to any contract alterations. I need to brief him. Kang Il-hyun knew everything. He had intercepted the hit and made a counter-offer—offering double the fee.

Ten million dollars. Roughly twelve billion won. An astronomical fortune that could buy a lifetime of absolute freedom.

Lost in the labyrinth of his thoughts, Jakyeong watched in silence as Ryun methodically smoothed antiseptic ointment over the scrapes on his palms.

"Feel any lighter?" Ryun asked quietly.

Jakyeong lifted his gaze. "What?"

"Putting a bullet in the man who ruined your childhood... Did it wash away the rot?"

Jakyeong didn't answer.

Ryun offered a gentle pat on his shoulder, then retrieved a clean duvet and set it over the cot. As he packed away the medical kit, his phone chimed with a message notification.

Glancing at the screen, a wide, genuine smile broke across Ryun’s rugged face. "Take a look at this."

He turned the screen toward Jakyeong.

Displayed in the photo was the group of children rescued from the processing plant, gathered together before the camera. Though their smiles were shy and subdued, the hollow terror that had haunted their eyes was gone. Beneath the image was a message from the parish shelter, letting them know the kids were settling in safely.

"Incredible kids," Ryun murmured fondly. "Enrolled in school and hitting the books already."

"That's a relief."

"The oldest girl’s name is Kim Joo-eun. Sharp as a tack—she's going to excel."

The desperate child who had once gripped a jagged stone to shield her companions was now holding a pencil instead. Seeing her in a neat school uniform brought a rare, unprompted smile to Jakyeong’s lips.

"I wired the funds you set aside straight to the parish account," Ryun added.

"Good."

"They asked for your contact info, but I gave them a polite excuse and deflected."

"Right."

"Want me to send updates whenever photos come in?"

Jakyeong deliberated for a moment, then gave a firm shake of his head. "No. Don't."

People belonged in the waters suited to them. Jakyeong belonged in the dark, blood-soaked trenches of the underworld; those children deserved to walk in the light, far away from the filth he inhabited.

Ryun tidied up the workbench, wished him a good night, and left the room.

Left alone in the quiet, Jakyeong sat on the edge of the mattress with his knees drawn to his chest, staring blankly into the shadows. Time slipped away as the first pale light of dawn began creeping over the horizon, accompanied by the steady drone of Ryun’s snoring from the adjoining room.

He lay down, willing himself to rest, but sleep eluded him. His muscles ached, and his mind was a storm of conflicting variables.

When exhaustion finally dragged him under, nightmares took hold. Choi Moon-sung and his dead son manifested as snarling demons, hunting him through a labyrinth of dark corridors. Just as he broke free from their grasp, Kang Il-hyun materialized from the mist with a handgun raised, putting a round straight through Jakyeong’s chest and sending him plummeting into a bottomless abyss.

Jakyeong snapped awake, drenched in cold sweat.

He sat up, checking the clock on the bedside table—barely three hours had passed. Morning light was pouring through the windows.

He reached for the bottle of water Ryun had left by the bed. Just as he cracked the seal, his encrypted phone chimed on the mattress.

[Have you considered my offer?]

Jakyeong clenched his jaw tight.

He tossed the phone aside without replying, but a follow-up message lit the screen a second later:

[If you've reached a decision, I'll come pick you up.]

Jakyeong’s fingertips hovered above the glass. He read the text over and over. Walking away from the contract was no longer an option—now that Kang Il-hyun held all the cards, every path forward was fraught with mortal danger.

Steeling his resolve, Jakyeong typed out his reply:

[Come get me. I'll be waiting.]
